Unnamed items must not identify the customer. No pricing in this file: studies are first-contact documents.

named.name: Sandymount Safaris
named.permission: Rykie Fourie (Reserve Executive) confirmed named use, 15 May 2026 (Notion: Sandymount Safaris - Case Study Source)
named.before: A consumer wireless service at about 3 Mbps down and 8 Mbps up, with the provider on site daily to swap IPs and reinstall equipment.
named.after: A Vodacom-backed 100 Mbps symmetrical link into the reserve, a CTTX-built main mast and two secondary masts, solar and lithium power, all monitored remotely.

outcomes.text: HD sport streams live at the lodges. Guest connectivity is no longer something the lodges think about.
Over 800 Mbps measured across the reserve's own backbone, linking the main lodge, Mountain Retreat and Samar.
Daily provider callouts went to zero. Every fault used to need a vehicle and a person; now the network is monitored remotely.
The reserve keeps adding systems on top of the backbone. In the client's words, they stopped doing speed tests.

unnamed.label: An Eastern Cape lodge near Addo
unnamed.text: Elephants broke out after 21:00 and staff had no effective way to coordinate. The requirement that came out of it: dependable communications after hours, across the areas where an incident can happen.

model.headline: One backbone for every driver of the business

drivers.name: Guest experience
drivers.text: Reliable Wi-Fi, booking and card payments at every lodge.

drivers.name: Staff communication
drivers.text: Lodges, HQ, rangers and maintenance on one network, day and night.

drivers.name: Security and operations
drivers.text: Cameras, gates, fence alarms and sensors on the same backbone, powered through load-shedding.

model.principle: Carrier connectivity comes in once. Everything on the property runs over infrastructure the reserve owns. New cameras, sensors and lodges plug in without a new provider contract.
